title: Enterprise Onboarding \u2014 Integration, Escalation, and QBR Playbook
author: Aisha Patel
body:
Overview
--------

Purpose
: This playbook unifies the enterprise onboarding steps for integration, escalation procedures, known issues & workarounds, and the Quarterly Business Review (QBR) template. It is intended for Customer Success (CS), Solutions Engineering (SE), Support, and Eng stakeholders involved in onboarding and ongoing account health for Redwood Inference enterprise customers.

Scope
: Applies to paid enterprise customers on Dedicated and Private (VPC/on‑prem) plans. Self‑serve hosted customers follow the lightweight onboarding checklist in the docs site.

Goals
- Reduce time-to-production for enterprise integrations to <= 6 weeks for standard use cases.
- Establish predictable 24/7 escalation targets and ownership during onboarding.
- Provide repeatable QBR artifacts that tie platform metrics to customer outcomes.

Owners and Roles
----------------
- Playbook owner: Aisha Patel (Customer Success).
- Integration owner (SE): Marco Ruiz.
- Escalation owner (SRE/Support): Liang Chen.
- Engineering escalation contact (runtime): eng-serving-runtime-oncall@redwood.com (PagerDuty: PD-REDWOOD-RUNTIME).
- Account executive & customer success: assigned per-contract (CS lead listed in customers CRM).

Prerequisites (before week 0)
- Contract signed + PO received.
- Security questionnaire completed (SSO/KMS/network requirements).
- Customer provides test dataset (PII scrubbed) and sample requests.
- Contact roster and escalation matrix from customer (names/emails/phone).

High-level Onboarding Phases (timeline)
--------------------------------------
1) Kickoff (Week 0)
   - 1.1 Kickoff meeting agenda: goals, success criteria, architecture, legal/security contacts, rollout timeline.
   - 1.2 Deliverables: onboarding plan, access list, test vectors.
2) Integration (Weeks 1–4)
   - 2.1 SDK/REST integration: provide quickstart repo, API key provisioning, example calls.
   - 2.2 Model selection & perf targets: recommend model variant, quantization profile (if Dedicated/Private), latency/cost targets.
   - 2.3 Network setup: IP allowlist, VPC peering or private endpoint, VPN details.
   - 2.4 Security & compliance: KMS/HSM integration, audit logging config, data retention settings.
   - 2.5 Pre-production validation: smoke tests, load test plan, synthetic traffic to evaluate latency and KV cache hit rates.
3) Rollout & Canary (Weeks 4–6)
   - 3.1 Canary strategy: 5% traffic for 48–72h, monitor latency P95/P99, error rates, token-cost delta vs baseline.
   - 3.2 Ramp plan: 5% -> 25% -> 50% -> 100% in increments with rollback gates.
4) Handover & QBR cadence (Week 6+)
   - 4.1 Handover document: architecture diagram, runbooks, relevant SLOs, contacts.
   - 4.2 Schedule first 30/60/90 day check-ins and baseline QBR cadence (quarterly).

Integration Checklist (minimum deliverables)
- API keys provisioned and scoped.
- Example end-to-end demo completed.
- Network connectivity validated (traceroute, curl to endpoint).
- Model variant pinned in production config.
- Batching and caching recommendations implemented for target latency.
- Security controls (KMS, VPC, RBAC) validated.
- Oncall contacts and escalation matrix populated in Support portal.

Technical Runbook Summaries (for SE + Support)
------------------------------------------------
1) Common validation commands\- curl examples:
  - curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate 
    -H 'Authorization: Bearer <KEY>' 
    -H 'Content-Type: application/json' 
    -d '{"model":"redwood-1-small","input":"Hello world"}'
2) Load test guidance\- Use the perf harness in the onboarding repo: scripts/load_test.sh --model redwood-1-small --concurrency 50 --duration 300
3) Logs and observability\- Where to find traces: Console -> Traces -> customer/<customer-id>. Include token-level cost breakdowns and P95/P99 latency charts.
4) Common metrics to monitor (SLOs to agree in kickoff)\- Availability: 99.9% (monthly).
- Latency P95 target: <= 300ms for < 1024 tokens (hosted), customized for Dedicated.
- Error rate (5xx): < 0.1% sustained.
- Token cost variance: <= 15% of agreed baseline during rollout.

Escalation Matrix & Process
---------------------------
Objective: ensure clear, fast routing of customer-impacting incidents during onboarding with measurable response times.

Severity definitions and response targets
- Sev 1 (Critical)
  - Definition: Production outage or customer cannot serve requests for key customer flows.
  - Initial response target: 15 minutes.
  - Remedy ETA target: 4 hours (workaround) / 24 hours (full fix) depending on root cause.
- Sev 2 (High)
  - Definition: Major degradation (P99 latency > target x2, significant cost regression, or repeated 5xx).
  - Initial response: 60 minutes.
  - Remedy ETA: 24–72 hours.
- Sev 3 (Medium)
  - Definition: Functional but non-critical issues (SDK bug, integration edge case).
  - Initial response: 8 business hours.
  - Remedy ETA: 7–30 days based on triage.

Escalation steps (ordered)
1) Support triage (Level 1): support@redwood.ai or support portal -> triage, KB article lookup.
2) Level 2 (SE oncall): If unresolved or technical deep-dive needed, escalate to SE: se-oncall@redwood.ai (PagerDuty: PD-SE).
3) Level 3 (Runtime Eng): For performance/runtime bugs, escalate to eng-serving-runtime-oncall@redwood.com (PagerDuty: PD-REDWOOD-RUNTIME).
4) Exec/Triage war room: If Sev1 unresolved after 2 hours, create a war room and notify leadership: cs-leads@redwood.com and eng-leads@redwood.com.

Required fields in a support ticket (template)
- Customer name and ID
- Impacted endpoint and request IDs (if available)
- Example request + response (including headers)
- Time window and GMT timestamps
- Recent config changes (model version, quantization, routing policy)
- Screenshot of console metrics (if relevant)

Known Issues & Workarounds (onboarding focus)
--------------------------------------------
1) Intermittent high P99 during initial cold-starts\- Symptom: Elevated P99 for first 30–60s after a burst.\- Workaround: Configure pre-warm concurrency (Dedicated) or use shorter canary windows and warm instances with synthetic traffic.
2) Token-cost spikes with long prompt prefixes\- Symptom: Unexpected high per‑request costs.\- Workaround: Use prefix caching and recommend client-side prompt truncation or summary techniques; set alert on token-cost delta > 20%.
3) Private deployment networking: MTU mismatches causing fragmented packets\- Symptom: Failed requests or TLS handshake issues.\- Workaround: Validate MTU on customer side to match instance network (typically 1500) and enable TCP MSS clamping if necessary.
4) KMS permission denials in restricted environments\- Symptom: Failed access to wrapped customer keys.\- Workaround: Validate service account IAM roles and provide the minimal policy snippet in the onboarding repo (examples/kms-policy.yaml).

Template snippets (examples)
--------------------------
- Example IAM policy (YAML):
```
# examples/kms-policy.yaml
Version: '2012-10-17'
Statement:
  - Effect: Allow
    Action:
      - kms:Decrypt
      - kms:Encrypt
    Resource: arn:aws:kms:us-west-2:123456789012:key/abcd-1234
```
- Example support ticket subject:
  "[Sev2] Customer <cust-name> high 5xx rate since 2027-03-09T22:00Z"

QBR Template & Health Check (quarterly)
-------------------------------------
Purpose: Align product/ops/CS to customer outcomes and identify platform-driven cost/latency/regression risks.

QBR agenda (60–90 minutes)
- 1) Executive summary (5 min): business impact and CS status.
- 2) Adoption metrics (10 min): API calls/day, active users, peak concurrency.
- 3) Performance & reliability (15 min): availability, P95/P99, error rates, token-cost trends.
- 4) Cost & optimization (10 min): unit costs, batching/caching gains, recommended quantization changes.
- 5) Security & compliance updates (10 min): audit logs, patching, certifications.
- 6) Roadmap & feature requests (10–20 min): product roadmap items of interest and scheduled changes.
- 7) Action items & owners (5–10 min): prioritized list with deadlines.

QBR deliverables (post-meeting)
- QBR slide deck (shared) with appendix of raw metrics CSV and runbook links.
- Action item tracker in shared project (Jira/Asana).
- Follow-up mini-check (30 days) for open high-priority items.

SLA & Contractual Notes (onboarding)
- Incident reporting must follow the escalation matrix.
- For Dedicated/Private customers, custom SLOs are documented in the contract appendix and operational playbooks delivered during handover.

Appendices
---------
- Links: onboarding repo: https://github.com/redwood-inference/onboarding-template
- Runbooks: Console -> Runbooks -> "Enterprise Onboarding" (runbook-id: RB-ENT-2026-001).
- Contact list for Escalations: support@redwood.ai, se-oncall@redwood.ai, eng-serving-runtime-oncall@redwood.com, cs-leads@redwood.com

Revision history
----------------
- 2025-10-15: Initial draft by Aisha Patel.
- 2026-06-02: Added known issues and workload-specific tuning recommendations. Reviewers: Marco Ruiz, Liang Chen.
- 2027-03-10: Updated escalation thresholds, QBR template, and added canary/ramp guidance.

If you are onboarding a new customer, follow the checklist in \"Integration Checklist\" and create the onboarding project in the CS workspace (template: \"enterprise-onboarding-template\"). For help or exceptions, contact the playbook owner (Aisha Patel).
